Subject: Post-call: minimal log window proposal & next steps for Phoenix HealthCare

Hi Aisha — thanks again for hopping on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of asks we heard on the call:
- Phoenix cannot accept persistent retention of conversational content or PII in logs; primary requirement is to avoid long-lived storage of user content.
- You’re open to a short, ephemeral debug window (for initial rollout) but want explicit TTL and access controls. Suggested range discussed: 0 hours (no logs) up to 48 hours for debugging.
- Need evidence for SOC 2, encryption at-rest/in-transit, and an operational process for deletion and audit of any debug artifacts.
- Data residency: production traffic must remain in US regions; EU residency not required for this initial pilot.

Redwood’s suggested path forward (one-page):
1) Pilot mode = 24-hour ephemeral logs (tokens/KV) with KMS-managed encryption and strict role-based access.
2) Debug access: audit-request model — logs retained for 24 hours by default; extraction or longer retention only with documented and time-limited engineering approval (ticketed).
3) Contract language: we can include a TTL clause and a point-in-time deletion SLA; we can also offer a hard 0-retention option if Phoenix requires it for production but accepts a short retained debug window in a staging environment.
4) Deliverables this week: redwood-security-brief.pdf (attached), draft MAP (phoenix-map-draft.xlsx), and a sample TTL contract clause (sample-ttl-clause.docx).

Next steps I propose:
- Aisha / Tom: confirm whether 24 hours is acceptable as a starting point for pilot, or if Phoenix needs 0 hours in prod and 24 hours only in staging.
- Phoenix legal: indicate preferred wording for deletion SLA and whether you need an explicit eradication certificate when we run a deletion event.
- Redwood (Marissa / Karthik): confirm technical feasibility and produce a brief one-pager of controls and escalation path by Tues.

If that works I’ll update the MAP and include a sample contract clause for your counsel to review.

Thanks — Ben

Ben — thanks for the recap and the materials. A few clarifications and firm asks from our side: 

1) Production requirement: Phoenix cannot accept any persistent storage of raw user content or PII — that includes KV cache snapshots that could reconstruct prompts or responses. Our legal team insists on either (a) 0 retention for production or (b) demonstrable technical guarantees that any persisted state is irrecoverable and redacted.
2) Short debug window: we are willing to consider a narrow debugging window but it must be <= 12 hours, with access only to a named set of engineers and with an auditable ticketing workflow.
3) Evidence needed: official SOC 2 Type II report (if available) or SOC 2 compliance letter, KMS integration details, copy of deletion procedure and sample audit logs showing a deletion event.
4) Residency: US-only for PHX data — please confirm region-level routing.

Legal asks: Tom will need sample contract language that guarantees deletion and a one-way confirmation when deletion is executed. We’ll also want to see what minimal redaction tooling Redwood can provide — e.g., automatic PII scrub or transforms before logs hit any tier of storage.

If Redwood can provide the SOC 2 artifact and a 12-hour debug window with role-based access + ticketed approvals, we can move forward with internal approvals and a PO in early December.

Regards,
Aisha

Subject: RE: internal: Phoenix ask — suggestions for concession

Ben / Karthik / Monica — internal notes to propose back to Phoenix: 

- Feasibility: 12-hour TTL for logs is technically feasible. We can implement a 12-hour ephemeral window that applies to both token logs and KV caches; it requires a couple of guardrails:
  * KMS-backed envelope keys per customer; keys rotated quarterly on request.
  * Explicit audit gating: only engineers with the role `debug_viewer` can submit a ticket in our ticketing system which triggers a short-lived signed URL to retrieve logs. All uses recorded in an immutable audit trail.
  * Automatic PII redaction layer: we can run an opt-in regex-based scrub on fields identified as PII prior to storing. Not a full NLP redaction, but effective for emails/SSNs/phone numbers.

- Legal / commercial: to avoid opening an open-ended engineering burden, propose a small one-time engineering fee for custom TTL/residency and a monthly surcharge while the custom policy is active. Alternatively, include the feature in Dedicated plans as an add-on.

- Contract language suggestion: add a TTL exhibit referencing the precise retention window, deletion SLA (within 48 hours of request for historical snapshots), and an audit evidence delivery clause.

Karthik — can you confirm the audit evidence we can provide (SOC artifact, sample deletion log, encryption key metadata)? If yes we should prepare the deliverable pack for Phoenix legal.

Marissa

Marissa / Team — confirmed:
- SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA; we can put Phoenix legal in touch with our compliance team and provide a redacted artifact.
- KMS details: we run customer envelope keys and can support a Phoenix-managed CMK via AWS KMS (or equivalent) for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we offer customer-wrapped keys.
- Deletion/erase evidence: we can provide a signed deletion event record that includes a timestamp, key identifier, and the job id that performed the purge. The job itself uses an irreversible delete on the persistent store and overwrites pointers to KV caches.

Operational ask: engineering needs a firm policy on the allowed debug window and whether Phoenix requires 0 retention in production. If Phoenix must have 0 in prod, we recommend: 0 in production + 12-hour staging debug window for rollout, with a documented migration plan.
